source.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses SAE feature-index non-identifiability and reports SAE transport results, but does not test feature splitting as dictionary size increases, whether split features partition inputs, or whether they form hierarchical families.
record.gate_note: The paper's SAE results concern transferring a dictionary across an exact signed-permutation gauge, not splitting across dictionary sizes. It also cites an SAE feature-overlap result from other work; that cited result is not recorded as a row.
record.test_reason: The paper is about signed-permutation gauge symmetry of RMSNorm residual streams. Its only SAE experiment transfers one fixed SAE across a known Bd basis change and reports reconstruction NMSE. It trains no SAEs of different dictionary sizes and measures no splitting, hierarchy, absorption or decomposition. Feature splitting appears only once, in a related-work list of causes of cross-seed SAE disagreement. That is a passing mention, so cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that RMSNorm residual coordinates are identifiable only up to signed permutation (Bd). They find that permutation-only alignment breaks transfer of coordinate-indexed artifacts, including SAEs, steering vectors and LoRA adapters. They also argue that SAE feature indices are non-canonical without gauge alignment. They draw no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The SAE experiment transfers a dictionary across a known signed-permutation gauge; it does not train and compare SAEs of increasing dictionary size.

fits_no_version.finding: TinyLlama-1.1B SAE transferred across an exact Bd gauge: NMSE 0.004 with Bd recovery vs 1.08 with signed-cost Sd recovery; the reference is 0.004.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferring SAE dictionaries across RMSNorm residual-stream reparameterizations requires signed-permutation, not permutation-only, alignment.

record.problems: The SAE evidence is a gauge-transfer test on TinyLlama-1.1B, not a dictionary-size sweep. The SAE dictionary size and uncertainty for the reconstruction values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant splitting results were reported. The feature-overlap figure attributed to Paulo and Belrose [2026] is cited from other work and was excluded.

untested.parts: All: no dictionary-size sweep, no coarse-to-fine replacement, no coverage or direction analysis.
All: no splitting analysis in large models or open SAE releases.
All: no feature families or hierarchy.
All: no parent/child latent firing, no size or sparsity variation.
All: no comparison of latents across SAE sizes.
All: the paper proves the SAE objective is gauge-invariant (Prop. E.9) but does not study splitting or alternative objectives such as Matryoshka.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the relation from discusses to cites_only: feature splitting is named once, in the Appendix N list of cross-seed disagreement sources. The Paulo and Belrose result (~30% SAE feature overlap across seeds) is cited work and is correctly excluded from the rows. Proposition E.9 and Corollary E.10 show that SAE indices are non-identifiable under feature permutation. This is a symmetry argument, not evidence on V5's claim about how latents decompose across dictionary sizes.

versions.untested_parts: Dictionary-size scaling, replacement of coarse features by finer features, input partitioning, and directional proximity.
Splitting at scale or across open SAE releases.
Nested feature families, geometric closeness, and correspondence to a concept hierarchy.
Parent-child firing overlap or effects of changing SAE size or sparsity.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and emergence of novel latents as dictionary size changes.
Whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective or changes under alternative objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.
